html:
The Watergate scandal began on 17 June 1972, when five men were caught breaking into the Democratic Party's offices at the Watergate building in Washington. They were linked to the campaign to re-elect President Richard Nixon.

Nixon and his aides tried to cover up the White House's role. Reporting by Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein of the Washington Post, a Senate inquiry and a special prosecutor slowly exposed it. Nixon had secretly taped his conversations, and the Supreme Court ordered him to hand over the tapes.

One tape showed that he had ordered the cover up. Facing impeachment, Nixon resigned on 9 August 1974, the only US president to do so. The scandal deepened distrust of government in the Cold War years and led to new laws on campaign money and secrecy, and to the suffix -gate for scandals.
sum: The Watergate scandal began on 17 June 1972, when five men were caught breaking into the Democratic Party's offices at the Watergate building in Washington. They were linked to the campaign to re-elect President Richard Nixon.
